messages:
maya: @support :rotating_light: Customer (tenant acme-inc) hitting /v1/rerank and getting 403s after they upgraded our SDK this morning. They say it worked yesterday. Posting minimal repro below.

support-bot: Auto-detected: error_code=model_id_deprecated; routing=ranker-catalog

jon: Can you paste the request + response body? Also which model id they used?

maya: Curl they used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-***' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/rerank-legacy-v1","queries":["what is the refund policy"],"candidates":["policy page","pricing page"]}'
```
Response: 403, body:
```json
{"error":"model_id_deprecated","message":"requested model id 'redwood/rerank-legacy-v1' has been retired","code":403}
```

carl: That model id was retired in Dec (migrated tenants to redwood/rerank-v2). We surface 403 to force explicit migration. Could the SDK be shipping a pinned id?

maya: Customer claims they updated to the latest SDK (0.9.8) this morning. They also run a proxy in front of calls. I'm worried the proxy is caching an old model override.

eng-runtime: Two quick checks: 1) tenant alias mapping in the catalog (we can confirm if acme-inc was auto-migrated) 2) any X-Model-Override header from their proxy. If the client sends an alias that resolves to the retired id, we'll 403.

jon: Maya can you ask them to curl with explicit model name 'redwood/rerank-v2' and see? Also ask for raw HTTP headers.

maya: Asked — they responded with headers snippet:
```
Authorization: Bearer sk-live-***
Content-Type: application/json
X-Client-SDK: acme-proxy/1.2.0
X-Model-Alias: tenant-ranker-default
```
They confirmed their proxy injects X-Model-Alias.

eng-runtime: Bingo. If tenant-ranker-default alias was pointed to the legacy id and the alias was never updated in their proxy config, we'll see this. We migrated alias targets but some clients cache the resolved model id locally. Two mitigations: 1) Update their proxy config to remove/replace X-Model-Alias, or 2) change their request to explicit model name (redwood/rerank-v2).

carl: I'll check the catalog entry for tenant-ranker-default for acme-inc and whether a compatibility redirect exists. If not, we can temporarily add a compatibility alias that points the alias to v2 for reads.

jon: Also, we should note for support: advise customers to clear SDK/proxy caches and confirm no hard-coded model ids in infra templates. We should add a KB article covering alias caching and migration.

maya: Customer tried explicit redwood/rerank-v2 and it works. They said clearing proxy cache fixed it too. They want a permanent signal in the response so their proxy can auto-update — currently only 403 with message.

eng-runtime: We intentionally return 403 to force explicit update. We can consider adding an optional header like X-Model-Replacement: redwood/rerank-v2 in the response to help proxies, but for security/UX we need product sign-off. Filing a follow-up with product.

jon: For now: (1) mark this tenant as resolved in the ticket (repro steps + fix), (2) doc sent to acme w/ steps, (3) follow-up for product to consider header signal.

maya: Customer confirmed resolution and will roll the proxy change across staging->prod. Closing on our side. :thumbsup:
